problem: Zero-shot VLN-CE agents usually keep spatial state via depth, pose or global coordinates. Recent geometry-constrained methods (DreamNav, LightZeroNav) use only short-term observation history or predicted views, so they cannot reliably confirm a place is a revisit, verify task progress, or recover after deviating.
motivation: Removing depth and coordinates improves cross-platform generalization and probes the spatial reasoning of foundation models. Without a persistent spatial state, however, long-horizon instruction following is fragile. The paper asks whether place identity and transitions can be kept purely from RGB and executed motion.
key_idea: Build a coordinate-free visual anchor graph (nodes are visual places, edges are executed motions) that supports approximate self-localization, sub-goal progress verification, and visual-revisitation backtracking in a zero-shot RGB-only VLN-CE agent.
insight: Backtracking through the anchor graph raises SR from 28.33 to 33.43 versus no graph/recovery, but lowers SPL (22.45 to 18.73). Deeper recovery hurts: 2 and 3 hops give SR 21.67 and 14.67, because errors compound along wrong branches, so a 1-hop budget is the best trade-off. The backbone ablation shows Qwen3.6-Plus outperforming GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6-sol, so the result depends on the VLM.
method: Decompose: a frozen LLM turns the instruction into ordered typed sub-goals (room_enter, portal_traverse, portal_stop) with entities, relations and a visual query.

SelectTarget: the agent rotates to capture six RGB views at 60° spacing; a VLM ranks them using traversability cues, then refines over ±30° views. GroundingDINO/SAM give a floor mask and a trackable point p.

ExecuteLocal: a KLT point tracker feeds a goal crop to the pretrained ViNT navigator. Arrival is triggered when the tracked point exits through the bottom of the image, and loss of the point signals failure.

BuildVisit/Associate: a six-view scan at each stop becomes a visit and is merged into an AnchorNode graph with TraversalEdges. Association is coarse-to-fine (global descriptor retrieval with cyclic view alignment, RANSAC ORB matching, semantic check) and returns SAME/NEW/AMBIGUOUS.
VerifyProgress: a VLM judges the visit against the sub-goal, outputting Commit_stage/Intermediate/Wrong/Uncertain. Only Commit advances the instruction.

Explore/Backtrack: rejected directions are stored and a per-anchor exploration budget applies. When it is exhausted or the branch is wrong, the agent retrieves stored views and trajectories, reuses ExecuteLocal to return, and accepts the return only if Associate gives SAME with the target anchor.

setting.backbone: Qwen3.6-Plus (frozen VLM/LLM) + pretrained ViNT + GroundingDINO + SAM + KLT tracking
setting.observation: monocular forward-facing RGB only (six-view scans by rotating in place); no depth, pose or odometry
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: move_forward 0.25 m, turn 10°, stop, 500-action limit
setting.privileged: none (simulator pose used only for evaluator-side distance)

numbers.extra: RGB-only, no depth or pose; 1-hop exploration budget

numbers_note: Real-world results are in success counts only (AGV 8/10 and 7/10; wheeled-legged 8/10 and 8/10) and are not included in the numbers list.
results: On the OpenNav 100-episode R2R-CE val-unseen subset, Navi-Agent reaches SR 33.4, OSR 48.3 and NE 5.79 with RGB only. This beats DreamNav (SR 32.8) and LightZeroNav (27.0), and also the depth/pose methods SmartWay (29.0) and InstructNav (31.0). SPL of 18.73 is below DreamNav (28.95) and LightZeroNav (20.00). Return SR is 80.3% and place-confirmation F1 is 0.71.
limitations: SPL is lower than several baselines because backtracking and six-view scans lengthen paths, and latency is high (8.3 s per target selection, 4.6 s per anchor construction).
Evaluation is on only 100 R2R-CE episodes, and the real-world tests are small (10 trials per task, one library).
Performance depends on the VLM backbone and degrades with deeper multi-hop recovery; place association is imperfect (F1 0.71).
